platform_specs.placement: Sponsored Content video ad, 9:16 vertical (mobile feed and vertical video feed)
platform_specs.aspect: 9:16. LinkedIn also accepts 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9, with a 5% aspect tolerance.
platform_specs.resolution: 1080x1920 is the maximum. The minimum is 360x640, and the help page names 720x1280 as recommended. Deliver 1080x1920.
platform_specs.fps: The help page says 'less than 30 FPS'. The marketing spec page says '30 frames per second' is recommended. 25 fps satisfies both readings. Never use 50 or 60.
platform_specs.video_codec: MP4 container, H.264 or VP8. File size 75 KB to 500 MB. No bitrate is published for ads; organic video is limited to 192 kbps to 30 Mbps.
platform_specs.audio: AAC or MPEG4, with a sample rate below 64 kHz.
platform_specs.max_length_or_notes: 3 s to 30 min. LinkedIn recommends 15 to 30 s and reports up to a 300% completion lift for 7 to 15 s videos. For 5 to 15 s videos it suggests trying loops 'similar to animated gifs'. Captions are optional and must be SRT. Third-party spec guides report that 9:16 ads serve only on mobile. That is not on LinkedIn's spec page, but it is a reason to also ship the 4:5 cut.
platform_specs.ui_overlay_safe_zone: LinkedIn publishes no overlay safe zone. A third-party measurement of the mobile vertical UI gives top 108 / bottom 320 / left 60 / right 120 px. That is unofficial, and the unified zone (288/672/120/300) contains it.

platform_specs.placement: Sponsored Content video ad, 4:5 feed (desktop and mobile)
platform_specs.resolution: 1080x1350 is the maximum. The minimum is 360x450, and 720x900 is named as recommended.
platform_specs.fps: The same rules as the 9:16 ad: below 30 per the help page, 30 recommended per the marketing page. Use 25 CFR.
platform_specs.video_codec: MP4, H.264 or VP8, 75 KB to 500 MB.
platform_specs.max_length_or_notes: 3 s to 30 min. Do not upload 1440x1800 here, because 1080x1350 is LinkedIn's 4:5 maximum.
platform_specs.ui_overlay_safe_zone: No official safe zone. The player overlays a mute toggle, a captions button and a progress bar along the bottom. Keep 65 px at the sides, 68 px at the top and 135 px at the bottom clear (derived). See feed_cut_4x5.

platform_specs.placement: Organic video post (member profile or Company Page)

platform_specs.video_codec: Members may upload MP4, MOV and others. Company Pages list MP4 with H264/AVC, VP8 or VP9, and no longer accept MOV. Bitrate 192 kbps to 30 Mbps. File size 75 KB to 5 GB.
platform_specs.audio: Pages list AAC among the supported types. No sample-rate rule is published for organic posts, so use the ad rule (below 64 kHz), which 48 kHz satisfies.
platform_specs.max_length_or_notes: Members: 3 s minimum from desktop, 2 s from mobile, 15 min maximum. Pages: 3 s to 10 min. LinkedIn reports 80% of feed video views happen with the sound off.

reading.words_per_second: Plan 2.5 words per second (about 150 wpm) for Dutch on-screen text over moving picture. The hard ceiling is 3.0 words per second (180 wpm) and 17 characters per second. The anchors: BBC subtitles run at 160-180 wpm, or 0.33-0.375 s per word. EBU says typical practice is no more than 140 wpm, because reading from a screen is 20-30% slower than print. Netflix's Dutch guide caps adult subtitles at 17 characters per second, 42 characters per line and two lines. The 2.5 figure sits at the EBU end because the text competes with the picture: BBC 4.3.4 says to allow more time when a lot is happening in the picture. TikTok's advice to show '5-10 words per second' is an outlier meant for skim text and does not suit B2B and government readers.
reading.min_on_screen_seconds_per_line: Hold each line for max(1.5 s, 0.4 s × the number of words in it), counted from when the last word is fully visible. That makes a 4-word line 1.6 s, a 6-word line 2.4 s and an 8-word line 3.2 s. A single-line card typically runs 2-3.5 s (EBU). The absolute floor is 0.83 s (Netflix: 5/6 s, 20 frames at 24 fps), and only a one- or two-word punch should go that short. Add about 1 s for a logo or label card (BBC 4.3.3), and hold longer when a line crosses a shot change or contains a long figure such as '12.353' (BBC 4.3.6 and 4.3.7). In 15 s that allows about 20-30 on-screen words in total, including the end card.

avoid: Any single app count without a decision on which one. The live English site says 22 apps and 36 in the diagram. The live Dutch site says 12 and 24. Slogans say twelve, llms.txt ~17, the /apps page '15 in the store', and cn-platform six. The fleet has 21 core apps, of which 19 are in the Nextcloud app store. The 22 includes Anonymiq, which is not a core app.
'21,744 downloads' or 'installs'. The figure is stale (generated 2026-06-08), counts GitHub release downloads under pre-rename ids, and /apps shows 21,677 'installs' from the same file.

'Enter a client once and your CRM, invoices and contracts all update' (openregister.mdx:42). In released code Shillinq keeps its own debtor record. What is shipped: the CRM client is your Nextcloud address-book contact.

'A quote your client signs lands straight in your books' (shillinq.mdx:114). Released Shillinq 0.5.0 listens for an OCA\DocuDesk event and probes isInstalled('docudesk'), while released Filinq 0.2.0 is OCA\Filinq, so it silently does nothing.
Payroll to journal entry, and payslips through Filinq (humaniq.mdx). Humaniq has no stable release and is not in the app store.
A request in the CRM becoming a case (Pipelinq to Dossiq). ADR-051 says zero code implements it.
Integriq's shared connection list. It landed 2026-09-14, after stable 0.4.4, and is beta only.
'Send to billing' as on by default. It is behind an admin switch that defaults to off (pipelinq SettingsService.php:209).
'Every app can hand its actions to an assistant'. Only some apps declare actions: Filinq 17, Pipelinq 9, and Shillinq, Dossiq and Decidiq 0.
Pre-built automations. The flow engine ships, but the customer draws each flow.

Version or status numbers from the site. AppsPreview shows OpenRegister 'STABLE v3.1' and Integriq 'BETA v1.2'. Detail pages show 'Beta v0.2' for OpenRegister and every app as Beta. The app store has OpenRegister 2.1.0 and Integriq 0.4.4.
'Maintained since 2019' for OpenRegister (repo created 2024-08-24), and 'Five years in' (founded 2019).
Four languages (nl/en/de/fr). The website ships English and Dutch only.

Apps that do not exist or are archived: Accountinq and Purchasinq (no repo), DeskDesk (archived). All three are in the committed design-system roster. Also 'Pipelinq = recruitment pipeline' (committed apps.html). It is a CRM.

Showing OpenAI, Claude, Mistral or other third-party logos as ConNext apps. The cn-platform example puts an 'OpenAI' hex among the 'six apps'. The site frames them as 'Open source we use, not own' and adapters.
Mixing the two managed-tenant prices: EN '€250 per component per month' vs NL '€250 per app per maand'.
Trademarks: the planning app is Planninq, never 'planiq' (an Anaplan trademark).

Trademarks: Nextcloud is cited, not claimed. Do not imply Nextcloud GmbH makes or endorses ConNext. Nextcloud blue #0082C9 is reserved for the 'Next' in the wordmark, the word Nextcloud and the workspace hex.
Trademarks: never 'Common Ground 2' or 'Common Ground Next'. The Conduction framing is 'Common Ground+'.
Spelling drift: the academy writes 'Connext' and the diagram 'ShillinQ'. The brand forms are ConNext and Shillinq.
Banned words and CTAs: 'ecosystem' when not concrete (taalgebruik §12.2), 'platform that', 'seamless', 'synergy', 'kernel', 'digital transformation'.
CTAs: 'Get started', 'Book a demo' and 'Try the demo' are banned. Use 'Install from the Nextcloud app store' and 'Request a demo from a partner'.
NLDS as a selling point.
Customer claims for SMB. All 43 client logos are public sector, and the 60/30/10 split is marked indicative.
Platform internals on screen (OpenRegister, schema, register, MCP, JSON, endpoint).
The em-dash in the home hero lede (index.mdx:33), per the no-em-dash voice rule.
